conviction_note: The sum of my findings is +3.7 and I emit +2.2 (a 1.5-point haircut), and the gap is deliberate: the dominant term (the Lockers strategic-review update, which the issuer contractually promised for THIS release) is bimodal rather than directional, and this print slot has twice punished the stock by roughly 15% (-17.82% on 2025-09-25, -14.20% on 2026-03-26) while paying only +3.01% for the one recent guidance confirmation (2026-05-22). So my point estimate is modestly positive and my band is very wide. What I am confident about is MAGNITUDE, not sign: the baseline's event_move_proxy_pct of 1.82% is the median of six cadence-estimated events and is wrong by roughly 8x against the two most recent full-results prints, and I verified on the AMF flux that Quadient has filed no information privilegiee / communique ad hoc since the 9 September quiet period began, so nothing is pre-released and the release carries the full information load into a 5-analyst, $0.5m/day name with unmeasured (probably wide) spread.

Q1 2026 printed -1.9% organic, i.e. inside but at the bottom of the range. There is no sourceable H1 2026 revenue/EBIT consensus: one French aggregator snippet implied ~EUR 1.12bn FY2026 revenue, which is ~8% above FY2025's EUR 1,036m and irreconcilable with a -2%/+2% organic guide plus an FX headwind, so I did not use it and no finding rests on a consensus number.

positioning_check: AMF positions courtes nettes: Quadient is NOT named on the register as of 2026-09-21, and the baseline's anchor_covered is false with state register_read_no_position. That is a truncated zero at the 0.5% disclosure threshold, not evidence that nobody is short -- I write no short-interest number. The consequence, per researcher_europe/LESSONS.md, is that priced_lean_pct (+0.155) is ENTIRELY the run-up term (lean_components: short_squeeze 0.0, short_building 0.0, runup 0.155), so this name's lean IS the free control the stage has to beat and cannot be beaten on that axis. The only visible disclosed-holder flow is therefore the AMF franchissement-de-seuils record, which I read as primary documents (finding 3): Janus Henderson Investors UK crossed UP through 5% on 2026-07-23 by buying on market, and crossed back DOWN below 5% on 2026-09-09 by selling 32,062 shares (1.8% of its holding), still holding 1,709,808 shares = 4.96%. Net over two months: a builder, marginally trimming. Published by the AMF on 2026-09-21, two days before the print.

findings.finding: Quadient contractually committed, in its own communique, to give a status update on the strategic review of its Lockers business ON THIS RELEASE (23 September 2026) -- with Rothschild & Co, Societe Generale and Darrois Villey already mandated at launch -- and only part of the deal option is still in the price: the stock rose +6.00% on the 20 July announcement and peaked at EUR 13.68 on 3 August (+14.0% vs EUR 12.00 pre-announcement) but sits at EUR 12.46 today, so roughly two thirds of the peak premium has bled out ahead of the one date the company itself named.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is exactly one prior instance of this line and it is the launch itself: 2026-07-20, the stock closed +6.00% at EUR 12.72 on 96,222 shares against a 60-day median of 37,606 (2.6x), then drifted to EUR 13.68 by 3 August. The line has never been tested by an UPDATE, which is why my band is wide in both directions: the modal outcome is 'process continues, no decision', a signed or near-signed disposal is the fat right tail, and 'we will retain and invest' is the left tail. The path to the equity is stated rather than assumed: net debt was EUR 682m at 31 January 2026 at 3.0x leverage including leasing (1.6x excluding), against a EUR 429m market capitalisation on 34,468,912 shares, so a disposal near the EUR 180m French estimate cuts net debt by about a quarter and removes the balance-sheet overhang that French coverage names as the single biggest concern on the name.
findings.original_quote: Quadient prevoit de faire un point sur cette revue strategique a l'occasion de la publication de ses resultats du premier semestre 2026, le 23 septembre 2026. Rothschild & Co, Societe Generale et Darrois Villey Maillot Brochier ont ete mandates en qualite de conseils financiers et juridique de Quadient dans le cadre des activites liees au processus de revue strategique. [Translation: Quadient expects to provide an update on this strategic review at the time of the publication of its first-half 2026 results, on 23 September 2026. Rothschild & Co, Societe Generale and Darrois Villey Maillot Brochier have been mandated as financial and legal advisers to Quadient in connection with the activities relating to the strategic review process.] Also, on the options: 'Le groupe examinera plusieurs options, allant de la poursuite du developpement en interne a l'ouverture du capital a un partenaire strategique ou financier, en passant par la cession de certaines activites geographiques ou une vente totale de la division.' [The group will examine several options, from continuing to develop it in-house, to opening the capital to a strategic or financial partner, to the sale of certain geographic operations or a full sale of the division.]
findings.why_not_priced: It is partly priced and I size it as such -- the launch is English wire copy and the stock paid +6% for it. What is not in the price is the dated update. If the market were positioned for an outcome on 23 September, the stock would not have given back two thirds of its announcement premium into the one date the company named, and the 5-day run-up would not be +0.48% with the 20-day at -3.11%; a market anticipating a disposal announcement bids a EUR 429m equity ahead of a EUR 180m asset decision rather than drifting from EUR 13.40 on 4 September to EUR 12.26 on 18 September. The AMF short register does not name the issuer, so there is no crowded short being squeezed and no positioning tell either way. With 5 analysts covering a name trading $0.5m a day, there is also no preview machine to put a probability-weighted disposal into the price the way there would be at 16-19 analysts.
findings.independence: Two independent corroborations. (1) Sector context from a different publisher: Axios Pro reported the same day that the review 'follows FedEx and Advent's $9.2 billion bid for European locker firm InPost', i.e. the European locker sector has an active strategic bidder -- https://www.axios.com/pro/supply-chain-deals/2026/07/20/quadient-inpost-parcel-locker-deals (2026-07-20). (2) An independent French sizing of the asset, DR Bourse 2026-07-21: 'Sur une valorisation de 15x l'EBITDA, l'activite Lockers pourrait etre cedee pour 180 M EUR' [At a 15x EBITDA valuation, the Lockers business could be sold for EUR 180m] -- https://drbourse.com/2026/07/21/quadient-une-revue-strategique-qui-pourrait-liberer-de-la-valeur/ . EUR 180m is 42% of the EUR 429m market capitalisation. NOTE THE DEPENDENCE WITH FINDING 4: finding 4 is a haircut on this finding's upside (the asset is trading worse than the sale narrative), not an independent negative, and this finding is sized well below the full option value partly for that reason.

findings.finding: Quadient voluntarily pre-disclosed a strongly positive operational datapoint about the quarter being reported -- Digital global bookings up more than 20% year on year like-for-like in Q2, with French e-invoicing bookings up more than ten-fold -- four weeks before the print and before the quiet period opened, which materially lowers the probability of the FY2026 guidance cut that is this stock's only demonstrated -15% trigger.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guidance line is the whole reaction function on this name and it is cleanly measured over three events. FY2025 guidance CUT at the H1 2025 print (filed 2025-09-24 after the close; 'FY 2025 revenue is now expected to decline by a low single digit on an organic basis', replacing 'acceleration in organic revenue growth') -> EUR 15.94 to EUR 13.10, -17.82%. FY2025 results with a EUR 124m Mail goodwill impairment (filed 2026-03-25 after the close) -> EUR 12.68 to EUR 10.88, -14.20%. FY2026 guidance CONFIRMED at Q1 (filed 2026-05-21 after the close) -> EUR 11.98 to EUR 12.34, +3.01%. So this stock pays roughly +3% for a confirmation and roughly -15% for a cut: sharply asymmetric, and the asymmetry is the reason my emitted move is far below the upside of my band.
findings.why_not_priced: It is partially priced -- the stock rose +3.26% on 92,795 shares (2.5x the 60-day median) on 24 August -- and then the whole of that move was given back: EUR 13.18 on 31 August to EUR 12.46 today, -5.5%. So the market bought the datapoint and then sold the print risk. What is NOT priced is its function as a negative signal about a guidance cut: managements four weeks from cutting a full-year guide do not usually publish '+20% bookings growth' under their own name. If the market had read it that way, the pre-print drift would not have been -8.5% from EUR 13.40 on 4 September to EUR 12.26 on 18 September. The French-language version of the same release exists in the AMF flux, so this is not a language gap -- it is an attention gap on a 5-analyst name, and the release was categorised 001006 (ordinary communique), not as regulated results information, which is exactly the classification that defeats a headline filter.
findings.independence: Corroborated by a different document and a different metric: the Q1 2026 release reports Digital annual recurring revenue of EUR 257m at end-Q1, +15.9% annualised organic -- https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/21/3299560/0/en/quadient-sa-q1-2026-revenue-strong-bookings-and-usage-growth-accelerating-digital-platform-adoption-fy-2026-guidance-confirmed.html (2026-05-21). And independently, the structural driver went live inside the reporting gap: Quadient filed on 2026-09-01 that it and its partners 'Support More Than 800,000 Entities as France's First Phase of E-Invoicing Reform Takes Effect', with Serensia by Quadient definitively approved by the DGFiP -- AMF flux record, PDF at https://fr.ftp.opendatasoft.com/datadila/INFOFI/MKW/2026/09/FCMKW130308_20260901.pdf (2026-09-01). Note the shared-document caveat with finding 4: both touch the 21 May Q1 release, but this finding's load is carried by the 24 August document.

findings.finding: The AMF published a 'franchissement de seuils' on Quadient on 21 September 2026 -- two days before the print, in French only, with no English wire version -- whose headline (a holder crossing DOWN through 5%) reads far more negative than the arithmetic inside it: Janus Henderson Investors UK sold only 32,062 shares, 1.8% of its holding, and still holds 1,709,808 shares or 4.96%, having crossed UP through 5% on 23 July by buying on market three sessions after the Lockers review was announced.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measurable on this name: the AMF short register has never named Quadient (anchor_covered false, register_read_no_position), so there is no disclosed-short history to read a squeeze or a cover off, and threshold declarations on a EUR 429m small cap do not normally carry a same-week price signature. I size it small for exactly that reason. Its value here is that it is the ONLY positioning anchor this name has, because the baseline's priced_lean_pct is 100% the run-up term.
findings.original_quote: la societe Janus Henderson Investors UK Limited ... a declare avoir franchi en baisse, le 9 septembre 2026, les seuils de 5% du capital et des droits de vote de la societe QUADIENT S.A. et detenir pour le compte desdits fonds et clients, 1 709 808 actions QUADIENT S.A. representant autant de droits de vote, soit 4,96% du capital et des droits de vote de cette societe. [Translation: Janus Henderson Investors UK Limited declared that it crossed downwards, on 9 September 2026, the thresholds of 5% of the capital and voting rights of QUADIENT S.A. and holds, on behalf of the said funds and clients, 1,709,808 QUADIENT S.A. shares carrying as many voting rights, i.e. 4.96% of the capital and voting rights of that company.] The paired upward crossing, AMF ref 226C1172 of 30 July 2026: 'a declare avoir franchi en hausse, le 23 juillet 2026, les seuils de 5% du capital et des droits de vote ... et detenir ... 1 741 870 actions ... soit 5,05% ... Ce franchissement de seuils resulte de [l']acquisition d[actions] QUADIENT S.A. sur le marche.' [declared that it crossed upwards, on 23 July 2026, the 5% thresholds ... and holds ... 1,741,870 shares ... i.e. 5.05% ... This threshold crossing results from the acquisition of QUADIENT S.A. shares on the market.]
findings.why_not_priced: It exists only in the AMF's French declaration archive and in no English wire, no broker note and no aggregator I could reach. If the market had read it, a 'largest disclosed holder cuts below 5% two days before results' headline on a EUR 429m name would have shown up as a down day on elevated volume on 21 or 22 September; instead the stock traded +1.14% on 50,186 shares and +0.48% on 14,420 shares, the latter being 38% of the 60-day median volume -- the two quietest sessions of the month. The 1.8% trim is also far too small to explain the one genuinely anomalous tape event in the window (553,716 shares on 18 September, 14.7x the median, at -1.13%), which I could not attribute and therefore score at zero.
findings.independence: The two paired declarations are separate AMF filings by the same declarant and I am treating them as ONE finding, not two. Independent corroboration of the direction of travel from a different source family: the AMF flux carries no information privilegiee / communique ad hoc from Quadient between the 9 September quiet-period start and 22 September -- the only filings in that span are these two declarations and a 14 September marketing release -- https://www.info-financiere.gouv.fr/api/explore/v2.1/catalog/datasets/flux-amf-new-prod/records?where=identificationsociete_iso_cd_isi%3D%27FR0000120560%27 . Nothing is pre-released, so no holder is trading on a leaked number.

findings.finding: The asset being put up for review is trading badly on the line a buyer pays for: Quadient's own Q1 2026 release discloses that Lockers non-recurring revenue fell 44.6% organically, taking the whole Lockers segment to -3.8% organic after +11.2% in H1 2025, and French coverage explicitly names this as the concern hanging over the 23 September checkpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The market has already been shown this exact number once and looked straight through it: the -44.6% was disclosed in the 21 May 2026 Q1 release and the stock rose +3.01% the next session, because subscription revenue in the same segment grew 18% organically and is now 80% of Lockers revenue against two thirds in FY2025. That is the single strongest argument for sizing this small, and it is why I cut it rather than carrying it at a full point. Its live bite is narrower: the FY2026 guide contains an explicit 'EBITDA margin above 10% in Lockers' target, up from 5.0% in FY2025, and a second weak hardware quarter puts that specific line at risk on a name that pays roughly -15% for a guidance cut.
findings.original_quote: les ventes de materiel des consignes ont chute de 44 % au premier trimestre [the lockers' hardware sales fell 44% in the first quarter] ... la revue strategique de cette activite fera l'objet d'un point d'etape le 23 septembre [the strategic review of this business will be the subject of a progress update on 23 September] ... Le principal point de vigilance tient a l'endettement, avec une dette nette de pres de 650 millions [The main point of concern is the debt, with net debt of nearly EUR 650m]
findings.why_not_priced: The number itself IS priced -- it was in the May release and the stock went up. What the French commentary adds, and the English coverage does not, is the link between the hardware collapse and the sale process: English Q1 coverage described it only as 'hardware sales were impacted by high comparison base', which is a comp story, while the French note frames it as the reason the 23 September checkpoint is a risk rather than a catalyst. I have deliberately NOT sized that reframing as new information about the quarter; I have sized it as a haircut on finding 1. If the market had already applied that haircut, the stock would not still be carrying +3.8% of the July announcement premium.
findings.independence: The -44.6% is confirmed in the primary company document, which is what makes it usable at all rather than a secondary claim: 'Lockers revenue amounted to EUR 24 million in first-quarter 2026, down 3.8% on an organic basis', with non-recurring revenue down 44.6% organically and subscription-related revenue up 18% -- https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/21/3299560/0/en/quadient-sa-q1-2026-revenue-strong-bookings-and-usage-growth-accelerating-digital-platform-adoption-fy-2026-guidance-confirmed.html (2026-05-21). NOT INDEPENDENT OF FINDING 1: this is the offsetting side of the same asset and I have netted it rather than counting it twice -- finding 1 is sized at +2.5 against a French estimate of EUR 180m (42% of market cap) precisely because this exists.

outside_window.finding: The actual announcement, signing or completion of a Lockers transaction, as opposed to a status update. The company itself refuses to date it: 'sans aucune certitude quant a l'issue, a la structure ou au calendrier d'une eventuelle operation' [with no certainty as to the outcome, the structure or the timing of any possible transaction]. If it lands after 24 September it is worth nothing to this ranking, and on a EUR 180m estimate against a EUR 429m market cap it is where most of the value of this situation sits.

Q3 2026 revenue, 1 December 2026 after the close, which is the first release that will carry any revenue from the French e-invoicing mandate: the mandate went live 1 September 2026, which is the start of Quadient's Q3 (fiscal year ends 31 January), so the H1 period being reported on 23 September ended 31 July and contains none of it.

searched_and_found_nothing: Les Echos, Investir, Boursier.com, Zonebourse and actusnews: not retried, per the measured 403-to-both-tools finding. I routed around them and note that Boursorama republishes Zonebourse wire copy, which is how I recovered the French communique body at https://www.boursorama.com/bourse/actualites/quadient-lance-une-revue-strategique-de-son-activite-lockers-d98d7f16c26a8c8558d45c43cc063b1f (HTTP 200).

No named bidder, no reported approach and no leak on the Lockers process in any French or English source since the 20 July launch. Searched in both languages including specific counterparties (InPost, Mondial Relay, Vinted Go). CEP Research's 22 July piece is paywalled to the first paragraph.

No information privilegiee / communique ad hoc from Quadient in the AMF regulated-information flux between the 9 September quiet-period start and 22 September. The only filings in that span are the two threshold declarations of 21 September and a 14 September analyst-award marketing release. So nothing about H1 has been pre-released -- this is a negative result that raises my magnitude rather than lowering it.

Could not attribute the one genuinely anomalous tape event: 553,716 shares on 2026-09-18, 14.7x the 60-day median of 37,606, at -1.13%. It is NOT the Euronext CAC-family September annual review -- Quadient appears in none of the additions or removals for SBF 120, CAC Mid 60, CAC Small or CAC All-Tradable, effective 21 September (https://mondovisione.com/media-and-resources/news/euronext-announces-2026-annual-review-results-of-the-cac-family-2026910) -- and no AMF declaration corresponds to it. A comparable 1,264,857-share day on 2026-05-29 suggests a recurring index weight/free-float rebalance rather than information. Unattributed, therefore scored at 0.

No sourceable H1 2026 or FY2026 consensus for revenue or EBIT from two agreeing places. A single French aggregator snippet gave ~EUR 1.12bn FY2026 revenue, which cannot be reconciled with a -2%/+2% organic guide on a FY2025 base of EUR 1,036m plus a EUR 12m-per-quarter FX headwind, so I discarded it. My bar is the company's own guidance instead, which is why no finding is sized off a consensus miss.
No plan social, restructuring, site closure or employment news at Quadient in the French national or regional press for 2026.
AMF positions courtes nettes: Quadient is absent from the register as of 2026-09-21. A truncated zero at the 0.5% threshold, not a measurement -- no short-interest finding is possible on this name.

No analyst rating change, downgrade or price-target cut published in the quiet period (9-22 September) that I could find in either language. Standing sell-side is stale and far above spot: consensus target EUR 19.40-20.00 against EUR 12.46.
baseline_tension: My net leans the same way as the baseline, and I want to be explicit that this is weak agreement and not confirmation: priced_lean_pct is +0.155, which lean_components shows is 100% the run-up term (short_squeeze 0.0, short_building 0.0, runup 0.155) because anchor_covered is false -- so on this name the lean and the free control -run_up_20d_pct (+3.11) are the same number wearing two hats, and agreeing with a +0.155 lean is agreeing with almost nothing. The real tension is elsewhere: the -3.11% twenty-day run-up and the -8.5% drift from EUR 13.40 on 4 September to EUR 12.26 on 18 September say the marginal holder de-risked into this print, which cuts AGAINST my positive net, and the only reason I stay positive is that the two things that drove the last two -15% prints (a guidance cut and a goodwill impairment) are both less likely than usual after a voluntary +20% bookings pre-disclosure on 24 August.
local_pass_note: Settled the session on a PRIMARY document instead of the vendor flag: the issuer's own French 2026 calendar carries '* Publication apres la cloture du marche', and the AMF flux timestamps on the two prior releases (2026-03-25T16:45 UTC and 2026-05-21T15:45 UTC) are both after the 17:35 Paris close. The baseline was right; it is now sourced.

ADDED finding 3, which exists only in French: the AMF franchissement-de-seuils pair showing Janus Henderson crossing up through 5% on 23 July (three sessions after the Lockers review) and back down on 9 September by only 32,062 shares, still at 4.96%. +0.3. On a name whose short register is a truncated zero this is the only positioning anchor there is, and the headline reads far worse than the document.

ADDED finding 4 from a French analysis piece (Decision Bourse, 25 August) which names the Lockers hardware collapse as the risk hanging over the 23 September checkpoint -- English Q1 coverage called it only a 'high comparison base'. I then verified the -44.6% in the primary company document rather than resting on the French secondary. -0.7, netted against finding 1 rather than counted twice.

SIZED finding 1 properly for the first time. The English pass knew the review existed; the French pass supplied the money: DR Bourse's 'l'activite Lockers pourrait etre cedee pour 180 M EUR' is 42% of the EUR 429m market cap, and net debt of EUR 682m at 3.0x is the overhang it would relieve. Finding 1 went from +2.0 to +2.5 (final, after lessons).

CORRECTED an overstatement in the frozen English draft. pre_local said the July announcement pop had 'fully round-tripped'; the tape says EUR 12.46 against EUR 12.00 on 17 July, so about two thirds of the PEAK premium has bled out but the stock is still +3.8% above the pre-announcement level. The finding now says the weaker, true thing.

Confirmed the 24 August bookings release exists in French in the AMF flux under category 001006, so finding 2 is an attention gap on a 5-analyst name and NOT a language gap. I said so rather than claiming local-only status it does not have.

Net effect: impact_sum 3.5 -> 2.8, findings 2 -> 4, expected_move 2.0 -> 1.8. The second pass LOWERED the sum slightly (the added negative outweighed the added positioning finding) and moved the CONTENT a lot -- it added the only positioning evidence available, supplied the valuation that makes finding 1 sizeable, and supplied the offsetting negative that stops finding 1 being sized off the full option value.
lessons_applied: 'anchor_covered false means priced_lean_pct IS the run-up, which is also the free control' -- rewrote positioning_check and baseline_tension to say this out loud, and reframed finding 3 from a curiosity into the only positioning anchor the name has. No size change to finding 3.

'A German ad-hoc filed before the print may have pre-released the number; the French analogue is information privilegiee' -- I had not checked. I did: the AMF flux carries no information privilegiee from Quadient in the 9-22 September quiet period. A negative result that RAISES magnitude, because the release carries the full information load. This is the main reason finding 1 went from +2.0 to +2.5 and expected_move from +1.8 to +2.2.

'Understatement is the hunters' systematic error; size on the name's own reaction distribution' -- the distribution is -17.82%, -14.20%, +3.01% on the last three prints against a baseline proxy of 1.82%. I widened finding 1's band from [-7.0,+13.0] to [-8.0,+14.0] and finding 2's from [-1.0,+4.0] to [-1.0,+4.5], and raised finding 2 from +1.5 to +1.6.

'Two findings that cannot both be true are resolved by you, now' and the warning about using one entity as evidence in both directions -- findings 1 and 4 are the two sides of the Lockers asset. Resolved by netting rather than by dropping: finding 4 cut from -1.0 to -0.7 (the market already looked through the -44.6% once, on 22 May, and rose 3%), and both records now state the dependence explicitly in independence.

'A one_off with no stated path to the guide or the multiple is sized at a fraction' -- finding 1 is not a one_off but it needed the same discipline, so its reaction_history field now carries the arithmetic path to the equity: EUR 180m against EUR 682m of net debt at 3.0x and a EUR 429m market cap.

'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series; a company-level number in a primary document beats a secondary' -- finding 4's load-bearing -44.6% is quoted from the French secondary that found it for me but verified in and attributed to the company's own Q1 release. Separately I discarded the ~EUR 1.12bn FY2026 revenue consensus snippet entirely rather than sizing a beat off an unverifiable aggregate, and capped nothing else on it because the bar is the company's own guide.

'Read the headline loosely and the URL strictly' -- re-checked the year in the URL path of every dated source: /2026/07/20/, /2026/08/24/, /2026/09/01/, /2026/05/21/, drbourse /2026/07/21/, decisionbourse /2026/08/25/, and the two AMF PDFs' _20260921 / _20260731 filename stamps. All 2026. No finding rests on a relabelled 2025 story.

'Keep findings inside the exit window' -- moved the actual Lockers transaction (undated, and where most of the value is) and the 1 December Q3 release into outside_window, leaving all four scored findings resolving on 2026-09-24.

'The hunter's own caveat has to reach the number' -- net of all the above, impact_sum 2.8 -> 3.7 and expected_move 1.8 -> 2.2, with the emitted move still 1.5 points BELOW the sum of the findings. The gap is the bimodality of the review update plus a print slot that has paid -15% twice running, and conviction_note names that gap and its size.
